label: sprites/fw_spit.spr: a sludge spit that splashes, animated

againstClass.words: flickers: more coherence from frame to frame

R1.reason: Reads as a splash: a ring of glow spreads outward from frame 1 to frame 4 and throws small spray droplets across the centre. That is the sludge spit splashing, animated, as the brief asks.

R2.reason: All eight frames are 64 by 64, and the border measures 0, so the edges are clean. The ring fills most of the frame by frames 3 and 4 and stays inside the frame in every frame.

R3.reason: The glow and droplets are a bright lime, yellow-green (frames 1 to 3 especially). The brief asks for green-grey sludge in Half-Life's muted palette, so this is more saturated and toxic-looking than asked. It is close, but clearly off.

R4.reason: Measured jitter is 1.62, outside the explosion class range of 1.04 to 1.48, so the motion flickers. The droplets jump to new positions between frames (frame 1 to 2, and again across frames 4 to 6) instead of drifting coherently. The rest holds: the ring grows then fades, the envelope peaks at 0.29 with first and last at 0 (within range), and the one-shot ends dark. The frame count of 8 is not held to a class measure here. Capped at 1 by the failed jitter measure.

R5.reason: Additive format with parallel type, 8 frames, under the name fw_spit.spr in sprites/. The brief names no type for this slot, so the type cannot be checked against a file it replaces; the format and name are valid for GoldSrc.
